title: Bounded comparison routine
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $o$ be an oracle on five deciders and bit strings, let $y$ be a bit string, and let $k$ be one of the two comparison labels. Suppose a fifteen-register state $st$ has all register values at most $B$ and its decoding-and-comparison scratch register is $0$. Starting with label the comparison routine for $k$ in phase $0$, register values $st$, and no result, the program reaches a configuration whose label is the success continuation if the comparison register selected by $k$ is at most the index register $i$, and otherwise is the failure continuation; the destination scratch register equals the minimum of that comparison-register value and $i$, with all other registers unchanged and no result. Every configuration strictly before the reached configuration satisfies the guard requiring all registers to be at most $B$ and the instruction-specific preconditions to hold.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ is an oracle on five deciders and bit strings
$k$ is one of the two comparison labels
$st$ has all fifteen registers at most $B
replaced:
Fix natural numbers $a,b,f,B$, a Boolean mode, an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to
each of five deciders and each bit string, an input bit string, and one of the two
comparison phases. Suppose the initial register state has every value at most $B$ and
its decoding-and-comparison scratch register is zero. Starting at phase $0$ of that
comparison routine reaches the appropriate success or failure continuation according as
the phase's comparison-register value is at most the index $i$ or is greater than $i$;
at the reached state, the scratch register equals the minimum of that
comparison-register value and $i$. Every preceding configuration satisfies the program's
guard requiring all registers to remain at most $B$ and all instruction-specific
preconditions to hold.
